# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
- Once Merlinus has joined your party, you will be prompted at the beginning of every single chapter whether or not you want to deploy him. Always select yes.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

# Playthrough Strategy

Pre-made strategy for the agent, plus the agent's own notes added as it plays. Every chapter has
its own section below with a **Recruits** table (pre-filled by the human) and an **Agent notes**
area (filled in by the agent). Broad, cross-chapter lessons go under **Broad strategy notes**.

## General Strategy

- Always select "yes" to accept side missions when offered the choice to do so.
- Once Merlinus has joined your party, you will be prompted at the beginning of every single chapter whether or not you want to deploy him. Always select yes.

## Recruiting Units

In each chapter, there are often units that appear as green units (uncontrollable allies) or red units (enemies). These units can often be recruited by executing the Talk action with a specific player-controlled unit, but there are some more complex conditions that have to be fulfilled in order to recruit some characters. For each chapter, you have been provided a list of the recruitable units that appear and the conditions that need to be fulfilled in order to recruit the character. You should try to recruit units if possible, but it is not a strict requirement.

The chapter sections below cover Lyn mode and Hector mode. Eliwood mode is not covered. Recruits are the same on normal and hard difficulty throughout the entire game, so use the list for your mode regardless of difficulty.

## Broad strategy notes

Cross-chapter lessons the agent adds as it plays. Append below.

content.content:
**Class ID is computable from the pointer — no ROM read needed.** Class structs are `0x54`
(84) bytes apart:

```
class ID = (class_ptr - 0x08BE015C) / 0x54
```

**Confirmed** by back-testing against a value derived independently in an earlier session: the
Lyn-mode Brigand pointer `0x08BE1410` yields exactly `0x39`, matching the Brigand ID already
in this document. Division came out exact on every pointer tested, which is itself evidence
the base and stride are right.

| Class ID | Class | Class pointer | Confidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `0x01` | Lord (Eliwood) | `0x08BE01B0` | Inferred |
| `0x02` | Lord (Lyn) | `0x08BE0204` | Inferred |
| `0x03` | Lord (Hector) | `0x08BE0258` | Inferred |
| `0x12` | — (heavy armour: HP 40, Def 17) | `0x08BE0744` | Unverified |
| `0x2A` | — (promoted: HP 36, Str/Skl 20) | `0x08BE0F24` | Unverified |
| `0x39` | Brigand | `0x08BE1410` | Inferred |

The three Lord IDs cross-validate nicely: slots 0/1/2 of the Ch.22 roster compute to classes
3/1/2 and carry roster indices 1/2/3, which is exactly Hector / Eliwood / Lyn in a Hector-mode
file.

### Character data struct

```
0x00  u16  name text ID
0x02  u16  description text ID
0x04  u8   character ID
0x05  u8   default class ID
0x06  u8   portrait ID
```

**Struct stride is `0x34` (52 bytes) — Confirmed.** Originally inferred from two brigands
sitting `0x34` apart; re-confirmed across a 29-unit roster in Ch.22, where consecutive
character pointers were consistently `0x34`-aligned.

**`char ID = (char_ptr - 0x08BDCE18) / 0x34` — Confirmed** (2026-09-27). Read straight from
ROM: for entries `0x00`–`0x07` and `0x2C`–`0x2F`, the struct's own ID byte at `+0x04` equals
1259:11. confirm: staff uses -1, staff moved to inventory slot 0, weapon rank +2
1638:0x28  u8[8] weapon ranks   -> inferred, see below
1758:and at `0x2A` on both brigands — consistent with an 8-byte rank array ordered
1775:| `+0x28` | 181 → 184 | weapon rank exp, +3 |
